questions.questionHtml:
🔥 GATE 2027 Original: Databases - Concurrency Control

Consider the following concurrent schedule $S$ involving three transactions $T_1, T_2, T_3$:
$$S: r_1(X);\; w_2(X);\; w_1(X);\; w_3(X);\; c_1;\; c_2;\; c_3$$
Which of the following statements is correct regarding schedule $S$?

💡 Detailed Concept & Solution:
1. Conflict Graph:
- $r_1(X) \rightarrow w_2(X) \implies T_1 \rightarrow T_2$
- $w_2(X) \rightarrow w_1(X) \implies T_2 \rightarrow T_1$
There is a cycle $T_1 \rightleftharpoons T_2$, so $S$ is NOT conflict serializable.
2. View Serializability check:
- Initial read of $X$: $T_1$ reads initial value.
- Final write of $X$: $T_3$ writes last.
- Write-Read pairs: none.
In serial order $T_2 \rightarrow T_1 \rightarrow T_3$:
- $T_1$ reads initial value (since $T_2$ only writes and doesn't affect $T_1$ if $T_1$ is before it? No, in $T_2 \rightarrow T_1$, $T_1$ would read $T_2$'s write!).
In $S$, $T_1$ reads initial value, so in any view equivalent serial schedule, $T_1$ must precede any writer of $X$, so $T_1$ must be first! But if $T_1$ is first, $T_1 \rightarrow T_2 \rightarrow T_3$, final write is $T_3$. However, in $S$, $w_1(X)$ occurs after $w_2(X)$, so $T_2$ does not overwrite $T_1$. Both $w_2$ and $w_1$ are blind writes overridden by $w_3$. Thus view equivalent to $T_2 \rightarrow T_1 \rightarrow T_3$.

options.html: $S$ is conflict serializable and view serializable
options.textHtml: $S$ is conflict serializable and view serializable

options.html: $S$ is NOT conflict serializable, but it is view serializable to serial schedule $T_1 \rightarrow T_2 \rightarrow T_3$
options.textHtml: $S$ is NOT conflict serializable, but it is view serializable to serial schedule $T_1 \rightarrow T_2 \rightarrow T_3$

A B+ tree index is built on a table with 1,000,000 records. Block size = 4096 bytes. Key size = 10 bytes, Block pointer = 6 bytes. What is the maximum number of keys an internal index node can store?

💡 Official Solution & Step-by-Step Derivation:
For internal node with $p$ block pointers and $p-1$ keys:
$p \times 6 + (p - 1) \times 10 \le 4096 \implies 16p - 10 \le 4096 \implies 16p \le 4106 \implies p \le 256.625 \implies p = 256$.
Maximum number of keys $= p - 1 = 256 - 1 = 255$.

The family of Context-Free Languages is NOT closed under which of the following operations?

💡 Official Solution & Step-by-Step Derivation:
Context-Free Languages are closed under Union, Concatenation, Kleene Star, Homomorphism, and Reversal. They are NOT closed under Intersection, Complement, or Set Difference.
